record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Main infimum problem on odd spheres
record.original_question: For each integer m > 1 and each r > 0, determine the number V(m,r) defined as the infimum of Vol(V) over all smooth vector fields V of constant length r on the odd-dimensional sphere S^{2m+1}, where Vol(V) is the volume of the submanifold V(S^{2m+1}) in the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric. If the infimum is attained, characterize all smooth length-r vector fields that attain it.

evidence.quote: The main open problem is to compute the infimum of the volume of smooth vector fields of constant length
and to characterise the smooth vector fields minimising the functional

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m > 1 be an integer and let r > 0 be a real number. Consider the unit sphere
S^{2m+1} = { x ∈ R^{2m+2} : |x| = 1 }
equipped with its round Riemannian metric induced from R^{2m+2}. Let TS^{2m+1} denote its tangent bundle, equipped with the Sasaki metric (the canonical Riemannian metric on TS^{2m+1} for which the horizontal and vertical distributions of the Levi-Civita connection are orthogonal and isometric to the base and fiber respectively).

A smooth vector field V on S^{2m+1} of constant length r is a smooth section V: S^{2m+1} → TS^{2m+1} with |V(x)| = r for all x. Such a section is an immersion of S^{2m+1} into TS^{2m+1}; let Vol(V) denote the (2m+1)-dimensional volume of the immersed submanifold V(S^{2m+1}) ⊂ (TS^{2m+1}, Sasaki metric), i.e.
Vol(V) = ∫_{S^{2m+1}} √det(I + (∇V)^T ∇V) dvol,
where ∇ is the Levi-Civita connection of S^{2m+1}.

Define
V(m, r) := inf { Vol(V) : V is a smooth vector field on S^{2m+1} of constant length r }.

(a) Determine the value of V(m, r) for every integer m > 1 and every r > 0.
(b) Decide whether this infimum is attained, and if so, characterize all smooth vector fields V of constant length r on S^{2m+1} for which Vol(V) = V(m, r).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of computing the infimum volume of unit (or constant length) smooth vector fields on the odd sphere S^{2m+1} is solved only in dimension three (Gluck–Ziller: Hopf vector fields minimize on S^3). For m > 1 (dimensions 5 and higher), Hopf fields are unstable; Pedersen exhibited smooth approximations with volume approaching that of a singular field, and conjectured (1993) that the infimum equals the volume of a singular field associated with a Pontryagin cycle and is not attained by smooth fields. This conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Poincaré index and the volume functional of unit vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Pedersen conjectured for m > 1 the infimum is reached by a singular field; the conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The Gluck-Ziller infimum problem on S^{2m+1} with m>1 is open.

status_evidence.title: On the volume of a unit vector field on the three-sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf vector fields minimize volume on S^3.
status_evidence.claim: Solved in dimension three by Gluck-Ziller; Hopf fields are minimizers.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Unit Hopf Vector Fields on Quotients of Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf vector fields are unstable critical points of the volume on S^{2m+1} for m ≥ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Hopf fields fail to minimize in higher dimensions, so the problem is qualitatively different.
